facts.statement: The only known species of Megalodytes is M. morejohni, known from fragmentary wingbones found in Middle Miocene marine strata in Kern County, California.
facts.quote: The only known species, M. morejohni, is known from fragmentary wingbones found in Middle Miocene-aged marine strata of Kern County, California.

facts.statement: Specimens from Japan that were originally assigned to Megalodytes have since been reclassified into the genus Annakacygna.
facts.quote: Other specimens from similarly aged material from Japan originally referred to Megalodytes is now referred to the genus Annakacygna.

facts.statement: Megalodytes is an extinct genus of waterfowl.
facts.quote: Megalodytes is an extinct genus of waterfowl.

facts.statement: Megalodytes belongs to the subfamily Cygninae.
Megalodytes is classified within the family Anatidae.
Megalodytes lived between 15.98 and 7.246 million years ago during the Langhian to Tortonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Langhian to Tortonian (15.98 to 7.246 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are two recorded fossil occurrences of Megalodytes in the Paleobiology Database.
